Scholarship was merely the transmission of what had been heard from the Lawgiver, and the teaching of unknown religious matters by way of oral transmission. It was persons of noble descent and group feeling, who supported Islam, who taught the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Prophet ﷺ, in the sense of transmitting traditions, not by way of professional instruction. For it was their own Book, revealed to the Messenger from among them, by which they were guided; Islam was their religion, for which they had fought and been killed, and by which they were distinguished and honoured among the nations. They were eager to transmit it and make it understood to the community; neither the reproach of pride nor the censure of haughtiness kept them from it. This is attested by the fact that the Prophet ﷺ sent his most important Companions with the Arab delegations to teach them the norms of Islam and the religious laws he had brought; he sent for this purpose some of the Ten and those after them. When Islam had become firmly established and the roots of the religion had struck deep, so that remote nations took it from those who possessed it, and its conditions changed with the passing of time, and the derivation of legal rules from texts became frequent because of the multitude of successive cases, a norm was needed to guard against error. Scholarship came to be a habit requiring instruction, and so it became one of the crafts and professions, as will be mentioned in the section on scholarship and instruction. The people of group feeling now occupied themselves with

81.id: kerajaan dan kekuasaan, maka ilmu diserahkan kepada orang lain selain mereka yang menegakkannya, dan ia menjadi profesi untuk mencari nafkah. Hidung orang-orang yang hidup mewah dan pemegang kekuasaan terangkat (enggan) untuk mengajar, dan menekuninya menjadi khusus bagi orang-orang lemah, dan penekunnya menjadi hina di mata pemilik 'ashabiyyah dan kerajaan. Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf, ayahnya termasuk pemuka dan bangsawan Tsaqif, dan kedudukan mereka dalam 'ashabiyyah Arab dan persaingan mereka dengan Quraisy dalam kemuliaan sudah engkau ketahui. Pengajarannya terhadap al-Qur'an tidaklah seperti keadaan pada masa ini, bahwa ia adalah profesi untuk mencari nafkah, tetapi seperti yang kami gambarkan tentang keadaan awal dalam Islam. Termasuk dalam bab ini juga apa yang dikhayalkan oleh para pembaca kitab-kitab sejarah ketika mendengar keadaan para hakim dan kepemimpinan mereka dalam peperangan dan memimpin pasukan; maka bisikan-bisikan cita-cita membawa mereka kepada kedudukan-kedudukan semacam itu, mereka mengira bahwa jabatan hakim pada masa ini sama seperti sebelumnya. Mereka mengira Ibnu Abi 'Amir, penguasa Hisyam yang memonopoli kekuasaan atasnya, dan Ibnu 'Abbad dari raja-raja Thawa'if di Seville, ketika mendengar bahwa ayah-ayah mereka adalah hakim, bahwa mereka seperti para hakim pada masa ini, dan mereka tidak menyadari perbedaan adat yang terjadi dalam kedudukan hakim, sebagaimana akan kami jelaskan dalam pasal tentang hakim dalam Kitab Pertama. Ibnu Abi 'Amir dan Ibnu 'Abbad berasal dari kabilah-kabilah Arab yang menegakkan negara Umawiyah di Andalusia dan pemilik 'ashabiyyah-nya, dan kedudukan mereka di dalamnya sudah diketahui. Mereka tidak meraih kepemimpinan dan kerajaan yang mereka raih melalui jabatan hakim seperti yang ada pada masa ini; jabatan hakim pada masa lalu adalah untuk pemilik 'ashabiyyah dari kabilah negara dan maula-maulanya, sebagaimana jabatan wazir pada masa kami di Maghrib. Lihatlah keluarnya mereka bersama pasukan dalam musim-musim panas (ekspedisi militer) dan pengangkatan mereka untuk urusan-urusan besar yang tidak diserahkan kecuali kepada orang yang memiliki kemampuan di dalamnya dengan 'ashabiyyah. Maka pendengar keliru dalam hal itu dan memahami keadaan-keadaan tidak sebagaimana mestinya. Yang paling banyak jatuh dalam kesalahan ini adalah orang-orang yang lemah pandangannya dari penduduk Andalusia pada masa ini,
81.en: royal authority and government, and scholarship was left to others who undertook it, and it became a profession by which to make a living. The noses of men of luxury and holders of power turned up at the idea of teaching, which became the special preserve of the weak, and those who practised it came to be despised by the people of group feeling and royal authority. Now, al-Hajjaj's father was one of the lords and nobles of Thaqif, and you know their position in Arab group feeling and their rivalry with the Quraysh in nobility. His teaching of the Qur'an was not, as it is at present, a profession for making a living, but was as we have described it in the early days of Islam. To this kind of error also belongs the notion of readers of historical works who hear about the position of judges and their leadership in war and command of armies; their ambitious whisperings lead them to aspire to similar positions, and they think that the office of judge at present is what it was before. When they hear that the fathers of Ibn Abi 'Amir, the regent who dominated Hisham, and Ibn 'Abbad, one of the 'party kings' of Seville, were judges, they think they were like the judges of today, and do not notice the change of custom in the position of judge, as we shall explain in the section on judges in the First Book. Ibn Abi 'Amir and Ibn 'Abbad belonged to the Arab tribes that supported the Umayyad dynasty in Spain and constituted its group feeling, and their position in it is known. They did not attain the leadership and royal authority they attained through the office of judge as it is at present; in olden times the office of judge was held by people of group feeling from the tribe of the dynasty and its clients, as the office of vizier is in our time in the Maghrib. Consider how they went out with the armies on the summer campaigns and were entrusted with great affairs which were entrusted only to those who had the means to accomplish them through group feeling. So the listener errs in this and interprets conditions other than they are. This error is most often committed nowadays by people of weak judgement among the inhabitants of Spain,

82.id: karena hilangnya 'ashabiyyah di negeri mereka sejak masa-masa yang jauh dengan lenyapnya bangsa Arab dan negara mereka di sana, dan keluarnya mereka dari kekuasaan pemilik 'ashabiyyah dari kalangan Barbar. Maka nasab-nasab Arab mereka tetap terjaga, tetapi sarana menuju kemuliaan berupa 'ashabiyyah dan saling tolong-menolong telah hilang; bahkan mereka menjadi bagian dari rakyat yang saling menelantarkan, yang diperbudak oleh penindasan dan terbiasa dengan kehinaan. Mereka mengira bahwa nasab-nasab mereka, dengan bergaul dengan negara, itulah yang memberi mereka kemenangan dan kekuasaan. Maka engkau mendapati pemilik profesi dan keterampilan di antara mereka berusaha untuk itu dan berupaya meraihnya. Adapun orang yang langsung mengalami keadaan kabilah-kabilah, 'ashabiyyah, dan negara-negara mereka di tepi barat (Afrika Utara), dan bagaimana penguasaan terjadi di antara bangsa-bangsa dan suku-suku, jarang sekali mereka keliru dalam hal itu dan salah dalam menilainya. Termasuk dalam bab ini juga apa yang ditempuh para sejarawan ketika menyebut negara-negara dan susunan raja-rajanya: mereka menyebutkan nama, nasab, ayah, ibu, istri-istri, gelar, cincin, hakim, hajib, dan wazirnya; semua itu adalah taklid kepada para sejarawan dua dinasti tanpa memahami tujuan-tujuan mereka. Para sejarawan pada masa itu menyusun sejarah mereka untuk para pemegang negara, dan anak-anak mereka ingin mengetahui perjalanan hidup leluhur mereka dan keadaan mereka agar dapat mengikuti jejak mereka dan menenun di atas pola mereka, bahkan dalam memilih orang-orang dari sisa-sisa negara mereka dan mengangkat jabatan-jabatan dan kedudukan-kedudukan untuk anak-anak orang-orang didikan dan kerabat mereka. Para hakim juga termasuk pemilik 'ashabiyyah negara dan setara dengan para wazir sebagaimana telah kami sebutkan kepadamu; maka mereka perlu menyebutkan semua itu. Adapun ketika negara-negara telah berbeda-beda dan masa-masa telah berjauhan, dan tujuan terbatas pada mengetahui raja-raja itu sendiri secara khusus, dan hubungan negara-negara satu sama lain dalam
82.en: for group feeling has disappeared in their country for many generations, with the disappearance of the Arabs and their dynasty there and their passing out of the control of the Berber people of group feeling. Their Arab genealogies have been preserved, but the means to power through group feeling and mutual support have been lost; indeed they have become part of the subject population who leave one another in the lurch, enslaved by oppression and accustomed to humiliation. They think that their genealogies, together with association with the dynasty, are what give them power and authority. So you find their craftsmen and artisans striving for that and seeking to attain it. Those, however, who have had direct experience of the conditions of the tribes, of group feeling and of dynasties on the western shore, and of how domination takes place among nations and clans, rarely err in this or misjudge it. To this category also belongs the procedure of historians when they mention dynasties and enumerate their rulers: they mention the name of each ruler, his ancestry, father and mother, wives, surname, seal ring, judge, chamberlain and vizier, all in blind imitation of the historians of the two dynasties, without understanding their purpose. The historians of that time composed their histories for members of the dynasty, whose children wished to know the lives and circumstances of their ancestors so that they could follow in their tracks and weave on their pattern, even in selecting men from the remnants of their dynasty and entrusting offices and positions to the descendants of their protégés and relatives. Judges, too, belonged to the group feeling of the dynasty and ranked with viziers, as we have mentioned to you, so they had to mention all that. But when dynasties became distinct and periods far apart, and the purpose came to be restricted to knowing the rulers themselves in particular and the relation of the dynasties to one another in

83.id: kekuatan dan kemenangannya, serta bangsa-bangsa yang menyaingi atau kalah darinya, maka apa faedahnya bagi seorang penulis pada masa ini menyebutkan anak-anak, istri-istri, ukiran cincin, gelar, hakim, wazir, dan hajib dari negara kuno yang tidak diketahui asal-usul, nasab, dan kedudukan mereka? Yang mendorong mereka melakukan itu hanyalah taklid, kelalaian terhadap tujuan-tujuan para penulis terdahulu, dan kealpaan dalam mencari tujuan-tujuan sejarah. Kecuali penyebutan para wazir yang pengaruhnya besar dan kabar-kabarnya mengalahkan (kabar) raja-raja, seperti al-Hajjaj, Bani al-Muhallab, keluarga Barmak, Bani Sahl bin Naubakht, Kafur al-Ikhsyidi, Ibnu Abi 'Amir, dan semisal mereka; maka tidak tercela mengisyaratkan ayah-ayah mereka dan menyinggung keadaan mereka, karena mereka tergolong dalam deretan raja-raja. Marilah kita sebutkan di sini suatu faedah yang dengannya kita tutup pembicaraan kita dalam pasal ini, yaitu bahwa sejarah hanyalah penyebutan kabar-kabar yang khusus bagi suatu masa atau generasi. Adapun penyebutan keadaan-keadaan umum bagi berbagai negeri, generasi, dan masa, itu adalah fondasi bagi sejarawan yang di atasnya dibangun sebagian besar tujuannya dan dengannya kabar-kabarnya menjadi jelas. Dahulu orang-orang menyusunnya secara tersendiri, sebagaimana dilakukan al-Mas'udi dalam kitab Muruj adz-Dzahab; ia menjelaskan di dalamnya keadaan bangsa-bangsa dan negeri-negeri pada masanya, pada abad ke-330-an H, di barat dan timur, menyebutkan aliran dan adat istiadat mereka, menggambarkan negeri-negeri, gunung-gunung, lautan, kerajaan-kerajaan, dan negara-negara, serta membedakan bangsa-bangsa Arab dan 'Ajam. Maka ia menjadi imam bagi para sejarawan yang mereka rujuk, dan pokok yang mereka andalkan dalam memastikan banyak kabar mereka. Kemudian datang al-Bakri sesudahnya dan melakukan hal serupa dalam al-Masalik wa al-Mamalik secara khusus tanpa keadaan-keadaan lainnya, karena bangsa-bangsa dan generasi-generasi pada masanya tidak banyak mengalami perpindahan dan perubahan besar. Adapun pada masa ini, yaitu akhir abad kedelapan, keadaan Maghrib yang kami saksikan telah berbalik dan berubah secara keseluruhan. Generasi-generasi Barbar yang merupakan penduduknya sejak dahulu telah digantikan oleh generasi-generasi Arab yang datang sejak abad kelima, yang mengalahkan dan menguasai mereka, merampas sebagian besar tanah air dari mereka, dan berbagi dengan mereka negeri-negeri yang tersisa dalam kekuasaan mereka. Ini ditambah dengan apa yang menimpa peradaban di timur dan barat pada pertengahan abad kedelapan ini berupa wabah tha'un yang dahsyat, yang menggerogoti bangsa-bangsa, melenyapkan penduduk generasi itu, dan melipat banyak keindahan
83.en: strength and dominance, and the nations that rivalled them or fell short of them, what use is it to an author at this time to mention the sons, wives, seal-ring inscription, surname, judge, vizier and chamberlain of an ancient dynasty whose origins, genealogies and positions are unknown? They do it only out of blind imitation, unawareness of the intentions of the early authors and disregard of the purpose of history. An exception is the mention of viziers whose influence was great and whose fame overshadowed that of the rulers, such as al-Hajjaj, the Banu al-Muhallab, the Barmecides, the Banu Sahl ibn Nawbakht, Kafur al-Ikhshidi, Ibn Abi 'Amir and their like; there is nothing wrong with alluding to their fathers and their circumstances, since they rank among the rulers. Let us mention here a useful point with which we conclude this section: history is the record of the information peculiar to a period or race. The discussion of general conditions of regions, races and periods constitutes the historian's foundation, on which most of his problems rest and by which his information is clarified. People used to devote separate works to it, as al-Mas'udi did in the Muruj adh-Dhahab, where he commented on the conditions of nations and regions in the West and East in his time, the 330s, mentioned their sects and customs, described the various countries, mountains, oceans, provinces and dynasties, and distinguished between Arab and non-Arab groups. He thus became the model for historians, to whom they refer, and the authority on which they rely in verifying much of their information. Then came al-Bakri after him, who did the same for routes and provinces exclusively, without the other conditions, because in his time not many transformations or great changes had occurred among the nations and races. In our time, however, at the end of the eighth century, the situation in the Maghrib, as we can observe, has taken a turn and changed entirely. The Berbers, the original population of the Maghrib, have been replaced by Arabs who began to come in the fifth century, who outnumbered and overpowered them, stripped them of most of their lands and obtained a share of the lands that remained in their possession. This was the situation until, in the middle of this eighth century, civilisation both in the East and in the West was visited by a destructive plague which devastated nations, caused populations to vanish and swallowed up many of the good things

84.id: peradaban dan menghapusnya. Ia datang kepada negara-negara pada saat ketuaannya dan mencapai batas akhir umurnya, maka ia menyusutkan naungannya, menumpulkan ketajamannya, melemahkan kekuasaannya, dan harta-hartanya runtuh menuju kepunahan dan kehancuran. Peradaban bumi rusak dengan rusaknya manusia; maka kota-kota dan bangunan-bangunan hancur, jalan-jalan dan tanda-tanda lenyap, rumah-rumah dan tempat-tempat tinggal kosong, negara-negara dan kabilah-kabilah melemah, dan penduduk berganti. Seakan-akan timur juga ditimpa hal serupa dengan yang menimpa barat, tetapi sesuai proporsi dan kadar peradabannya. Seakan-akan lisan alam semesta menyeru di dunia untuk kelesuan dan pengerutan, lalu ia segera menjawab. Dan Allah-lah pewaris bumi dan semua yang ada di atasnya. Jika keadaan berubah secara keseluruhan, seakan-akan makhluk telah berubah dari asalnya dan seluruh dunia telah berpindah, seakan-akan ia adalah ciptaan baru, kejadian yang dimulai lagi, dan dunia yang baru diadakan. Maka pada masa ini dibutuhkan orang yang mencatat keadaan makhluk dan negeri-negeri, generasi-generasinya, serta adat istiadat dan aliran yang telah berubah bagi penduduknya, dan mengikuti jalan al-Mas'udi pada zamannya, agar menjadi pokok yang diteladani oleh para sejarawan yang datang sesudahnya. Aku akan menyebutkan dalam kitabku ini sebisaku tentang hal itu di wilayah Maghrib ini, baik secara terang maupun tercakup dalam kabar-kabarnya dan secara isyarat, karena tujuanku dalam menyusun kitab ini khusus tentang Maghrib, keadaan generasi-generasi dan bangsa-bangsanya, serta penyebutan kerajaan-kerajaan dan negara-negaranya, tidak tentang wilayah-wilayah lain, karena aku tidak mengetahui keadaan timur dan bangsa-bangsanya, dan kabar-kabar yang dinukil tidak memenuhi hakikat apa yang aku inginkan darinya. Al-Mas'udi hanya dapat menyempurnakannya karena jauhnya perjalanannya dan berkelilingnya ia di negeri-negeri, sebagaimana ia sebutkan dalam kitabnya; meski demikian, ketika ia menyebut Maghrib, ia kurang dalam melengkapi keadaannya. "Dan di atas setiap orang yang berilmu ada yang lebih mengetahui" (QS. Yusuf: 76), dan tempat kembali seluruh ilmu adalah kepada Allah. Manusia lemah dan kurang, dan pengakuan (akan hal itu) adalah keharusan. Siapa yang mendapat pertolongan Allah, akan dimudahkan jalan-jalannya dan berhasil usaha-usaha serta tuntutan-tuntutannya. Kami, dengan pertolongan Allah, akan memulai apa yang kami maksudkan dari tujuan-tujuan penyusunan kitab ini; Allah-lah yang meluruskan dan menolong, dan kepada-Nya kami bertawakal. Masih tersisa bagi kami untuk mendahulukan sebuah pendahuluan tentang cara menuliskan huruf-huruf yang tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Arab jika muncul dalam kitab kami ini.
84.en: of civilisation and wiped them out. It overtook the dynasties at the time of their senility, when they had reached the limit of their duration; it lessened their power, curtailed their influence and weakened their authority, and their wealth headed for annihilation and dissolution. Civilisation decreased with the decrease of mankind. Cities and buildings were laid waste, roads and way signs were obliterated, settlements and mansions became empty, dynasties and tribes grew weak, and the entire inhabited world changed. The East, it seems, was similarly visited, though in accordance with and in proportion to its civilisation. It was as if the voice of existence in the world had called out for oblivion and restriction, and the world had responded to its call. Allah inherits the earth and whoever is upon it. When there is a general change of conditions, it is as if the entire creation had changed and the whole world been altered, as if it were a new and repeated creation, a world brought into existence anew. Therefore there is need at this time that someone should systematically set down the situation of the world among all regions and races, as well as the customs and sectarian beliefs that have changed for their adherents, doing for this age what al-Mas'udi did for his, so that it may serve as a model for future historians to follow. In this book of mine I shall discuss as much of this as will be possible for me here in the Maghrib, either explicitly or implicitly in connection with its history and by allusion, because my intention in this work is restricted to the Maghrib, the circumstances of its races and nations, and its subjects and dynasties, to the exclusion of any other region. This restriction is due to my lack of knowledge of conditions in the East and among its nations, and to the fact that secondhand information would not give the essence of what I am after. Al-Mas'udi's work was complete because of his many travels and journeys through the countries, as he mentioned in his book; yet when he spoke of the Maghrib his account was incomplete. 'Above everyone possessed of knowledge there is one more knowing' (Qur'an 12:76), and all knowledge ultimately goes back to Allah. Man is weak and deficient, and admission of this is a necessary duty. He whom Allah helps finds his ways easy and his efforts and quests successful. With Allah's help we shall now begin what we intended for this work; Allah gives guidance and help, and in Him we trust. It remains for us to say something about the method of writing letters that are not part of the Arabic language when they occur in our book.
